question: What happens when two Olympic swimmers touch the wall in exactly the same hundredth of a second?
answer: They share the medal. Swimming stopped separating racers by thousandths after 1972, when Gunnar Larsson won the Olympic 400 m medley by 0.002 seconds. So ties stand: at Sydney in 2000, Anthony Ervin and Gary Hall Jr both clocked 21.98 in the 50 m freestyle, and two gold medals were awarded.
move: When the measurement cannot separate two results, do not invent a winner.
reference: Organising Committee for the Games of the XXth Olympiad, Official Report, Munich, 1974
